title: The Rabbit and the Arrogant Lion
summary: An arrogant lion eats a forest animal every day. The little rabbit finds a way to stop him.
moral: Cleverness can overcome strength, and arrogance makes a person easily fooled by their own reflection.
pages: In a forest lived a very arrogant lion. Every day he ate any animal he met. 'I am the king of the forest!' the lion roared. All the animals lived in fear.
The animals gathered and agreed to go to the lion. 'King, we will send one animal each day for your food, as long as you no longer hunt us.' The lion agreed. That day, it was the rabbit's turn to go.
The rabbit did not hurry. He walked slowly, stopped under a tree, and reached the lion's place only when the sun was high. The lion waited with a hungry stomach, very angry.

'Why are you late?' growled the lion. The rabbit answered, 'Forgive me, King. On the way I was stopped by another lion who claims to be king of the forest. He held back my friends and said he is stronger than you!' The lion roared with rage.
'Show me where that lion is!' barked the lion. The rabbit led him to a deep old well. 'He is hiding down there, King,' said the rabbit, pointing down.
The lion peeped into the well and saw another lion staring back with a fierce face. He roared, and the lion below roared too. Furious, the lion leapt into the well to pounce on him.
Splash! It turned out that what he saw was only his own reflection. The lion never appeared again. The animals cheered and thanked the clever rabbit. The forest was peaceful once more. The end.
